_voice: Use the polite gender-neutral "ku" (never the gendered kai/ke), Latin script (Boko).
_style: Address the user always with the polite plural “ku” (ku, ku-/kun/kuna, -ku: “Ku ajiye”, “bishiyarku”), never the gendered kai/ke, ka/ki, -ka/-ki; when speaking about the couple as a unit use “ku biyu” (“bishiyarku ta ku biyu”, “tare”), and inside messages the user sends to the partner (pings, reactions) also use “ku” so the text stays gender-neutral (“Ina tunaninku”). The other person is “abokin zamanku” (treat “abokin zama” as a generic, gender-unmarked term; never saurayi/budurwa, miji/mata); because Hausa third-person singular is gendered (shi/ita, ya/ta, -sa/-ta), avoid pronouns for the partner by repeating the name placeholder %@, using “abokin zamanku”, or rephrasing with impersonal “an …”/“za a …” constructions (“An shayar da lambun” instead of “Ya/Ta shayar…”). The partner name placeholder %@ is never inflected or given a suffix (no %@n, %@r, no linking -n/-r attached to it): rephrase so the name stands alone (“Saƙo daga %@” rather than “Saƙon %@”). Use curly double quotes “ ” for outer and single ‘ ’ for inner quotes, the single-character ellipsis …, no space before ? ! : ;, keep “ · ”, \n, emoji and all placeholders (%@, %lld, %1$@) exactly as in English. Write Latin script (Boko) with the hooked letters ɓ ɗ ƙ and the apostrophe ʼ written as a straight ' in ƴ/'y (“'ya'ya”, “ma'aurata”); never replace ɓ ɗ ƙ with b d k. Numbers use Western digits; dates follow the device locale (day before month, e.g. “14 ga Nuwamba”, “ranar …”); times are 24-hour or as the system formats them. Buttons and actions are short imperatives without “ku” or “don Allah” (“Ajiye”, “Aika wasiƙa”, “Sake gwadawa”); titles, tabs, chips and buttons use sentence case (capital on the first word only) except proper names like Coupley, Premium and AI. Plural categories are ["one","other"]: “one” uses the singular noun (“kwana %lld”), “other” the plural or the invariant counted form (“kwanaki %lld”); Hausa usually puts the number after the noun. Tone: warm, light, kind, natural everyday Hausa (Kano standard), never cheesy or word-for-word.
